title: SPOT: Span-level Pause-of-Thought for Efficient and Interpretable Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Verbose explicit chain-of-thought traces improve reasoning performance but impose high inference cost.

gap.claim: Existing latent-reasoning methods face insufficient span-level semantic coverage and limited interpretability because of rigid alignment and unconstrained latent-state construction.

contributions.claim: SPOT compresses explicit chain-of-thought into compact latent tokens without enforcing a fixed response template.
Span-level Semantic Alignment uses a Sinkhorn optimal-transport objective to softly match tokens to the semantics of entire reasoning segments.
Frozen-Head Decoding Constraint keeps latent states directly decodable as token distributions under the frozen pretrained language-model head.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the reported main reasoning benchmarks, SPOT improves accuracy by 2.3 points on average and reduces generated tokens by 37.5%.
The authors report faithful semantic interpretations of the latent reasoning process.

narrative_sequence.summary: Explicit chain-of-thought improves reasoning but is costly, while concise prompting and pruning mainly truncate output.
Latent reasoning is promising but prior methods have rigid point-to-point alignment and poor interpretability.
SPOT compresses explicit chain-of-thought into latent tokens using span-level semantic alignment.
Frozen-head decoding supports readable interpretations, while two-stage training enables controllable implicit reasoning intensity.
The authors report improved accuracy, fewer generated tokens, and faithful semantic interpretations.

source_observation.claim: Matching latent representations to entire reasoning spans is presented as more flexible than matching only to step-end representations.

interpretation.claim: Reasoning representations may benefit from alignment objectives that accommodate dense, variable-length semantic units.

application.claim: For latent sequence compression, consider soft span-level alignment when individual endpoint targets underrepresent intermediate semantics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether span-level alignment is preferable across tasks or reasoning domains.

source_observation.claim: Constraining latent states to remain decodable under a frozen language-model head is reported to enable readable keyword interpretations.

interpretation.claim: A fixed pretrained decoding interface can provide an interpretability constraint for latent reasoning.

application.claim: When interpretability matters, constrain learned latent states through an existing frozen decoder where feasible.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how faithfully the keyword interpretations reflect the complete latent reasoning process.

unknowns: The benchmark names, datasets, baselines, and evaluation protocol are not specified.
The abstract does not define the omitted object in the phrase “without direct token-level supervision on .”
Training configuration and computational cost are not specified.
